**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include crashed launchers when computing idle eligibility**

If a worktree's first launcher dies through SIGKILL or a host crash, its dead attachment remains but no `last_detach` exists. Planning calls `live_attachments(..., prune=False)`, then skips this instance because its detach age is `None`. The pruning code that creates `last_detach` runs only after a candidate reaches `_reap_one`, so repeated automatic or explicit reaps never clean up these idle sidecars while the checkout exists. Derive idle eligibility from dead attachment timestamps without mutating the dry-run plan, then prune under the instance lock.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Load the target repository's catalog when initializing via --repo**

When `init --repo <target>` runs outside the target checkout and the target has a repo-local `mcp_catalog.yaml`, initialization still calls `_load_catalog()` without `repo_path`, selecting the caller's catalog or the bundled default instead. Target-only `--with` services consequently fail as unknown, and differing defaults generate configuration and leases from the wrong catalog. This also disagrees with the launcher, which explicitly loads the target checkout's catalog. Pass the resolved target to catalog loading before rendering configuration or allocating ports.

This path uses the wrong filename case: the tracked document is `.claude/claude.md`, and `.claude/CLAUDE.md` does not exist on a case-sensitive checkout. The new parametrized test raises `FileNotFoundError` on Linux before checking the document, even though it passes on a case-insensitive macOS filesystem. Use the tracked lowercase path.

`native-hooks register` emits SessionEnd hooks without a timeout, while the new handler can spend up to 45 seconds reaping before saving session history. Registrations in other projects or global settings can therefore be terminated by the short default budget before cleanup and persistence finish. Add `timeout: 60` for SessionEnd, including existing Dopemux registrations that lack it.

`_url_is_repairable()` accepts any URL containing `${...}`, so this guard allows remote or credential-bearing endpoints to be replaced with local launchers and lose their URL/env. Examples include `https://remote.example:${REMOTE_PORT:-443}/sse` and `http://user:${PASSWORD}@localhost:3005/sse`. Check hostname and userinfo even for templated URLs, preserving entries whose destination cannot be proven local.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recover committed migrations before replaying tenant provisioning**

If provisioning stops after migration SQL commits but before `on_migration(name)` persists its checkpoint—for example, through SIGKILL or a state-file write failure—the next start replays that committed migration. `_remaining_migrations()` consults only the local checkpoint, while migrations 001 and 002 contain non-idempotent `CREATE VIEW`/`CREATE TRIGGER` statements. Consequently, every subsequent init/start fails with an already-exists error instead of resuming provisioning. Reconcile against the migration metadata committed in PostgreSQL before choosing which migrations to replay.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Normalize explicit init targets to their git worktree root**

When `init --repo` receives a directory inside a checkout, such as `--repo ./src`, this branch retains that subdirectory even though `resolve_project_identity()` resolves the enclosing worktree. Initialization then looks for the catalog, allocates leases, and writes `.mcp.json` and `.envrc.dopemux-mcp` relative to the subdirectory. The launcher instead normalizes its root with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and requires `.mcp.json` there, so the generated configuration cannot launch successfully. Normalize the explicit target to `identity.worktree_root` before catalog lookup, allocation, and file writes.

This PR-scoped proof still certifies `30b0fdec9`, but the current head is `e49a1c8e`, whose commit changes tenant-provisioning logic in `conport_tenant.py`. These are substantive successors, not the proof-only delta allowed by local audit acceptance, so the earlier audit cannot authenticate the current implementation. Run a fresh independent audit after the final code freeze, then regenerate and sign the PR-scoped proof; simply changing this SHA would misrepresent the audited subject.

These variables are also required by dopemux commands that can start `dope-context`. Those paths deliberately pass `host_path_defaults=False` (for example, `mcp_commands.py:605,774`) to preserve the required workspace-mount guard, so leaving them blank can still make `dopemux mcp` startup fail. Qualify this note rather than saying that only raw Compose requires them.

A hostname placeholder's default does not prove that the endpoint is local. For example, with `CONPORT_HOST=remote.example`, `http://${CONPORT_HOST:-localhost}:3005/sse` still returns `True` here. The launcher repair then deletes that operator-selected remote URL and replaces it with a local stdio connection. Preserve hostname/userinfo placeholders regardless of their defaults; neutralize only port-position placeholders for locality checks, and update the corresponding test expectation.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recover interrupted idle reaps while the checkout still exists**

If an idle reap is interrupted after removing its last container but before releasing state, or `_release_state()` fails, subsequent reaps cannot finish cleanup while the checkout exists. Container discovery no longer finds the instance, and this state-only recovery branch unconditionally skips existing worktrees, even when `last_detach` exceeds the idle threshold. Active port leases, stale running records, and retained runtime files therefore remain indefinitely unless the checkout is deleted or relaunched. Apply the idle-eligibility predicate to state-only candidates too, retaining the attachment check and locked revalidation.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Revalidate container-backed candidates under the instance lock**

If a CLI restart recreates an idle sidecar between planning and lock acquisition, this check skips reinspection because the candidate contains old container IDs. Restart preserves `last_detach`, so eligibility still passes; `_stop_and_remove()` treats the missing old containers as successfully removed, then `_release_state()` releases the replacement's leases, marks its running record stopped, and removes its runtime directory while the replacement remains alive. A fake-runner reproduction confirmed this path performs no pair inspection and reports the instance reaped. Reinspect container-backed candidates under the lock too, and reject or refresh plans whose container set changed before releasing state.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match reaped leases using the allocator's identity convention**

For leases created by either `init` or the launcher, `allocate_ports()` defaults `project_id` to `Path(project_root).name`, whereas reap candidates carry the hashed `ProjectIdentity.project_id`. This comparison therefore skips those leases even when their worktree paths match. Reaping still removes the containers and runtime directory and marks instances stopped, but leaves their ports actively reserved; `_has_active_leases()` repeats the same mismatched comparison, preventing subsequent state-only recovery. Repeated worktree churn consequently consumes the available port range. Use the registry's identity-matching convention, which already accommodates these aliases, consistently in release and recovery checks.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reacquire leases for ports supplied by the checkout envrc**

After `init` followed by `stop`, the port leases are released but `.envrc.dopemux-mcp` remains. On the next start—including a launcher's cold start—all port variables are present, so this branch returns without reacquiring leases even with `allocate=True`. An isolated reproduction returns the original port with zero active leases. The service can consequently start without a reservation, allowing another worktree's concurrent allocation to claim that port before Compose publishes it and causing a bind failure. Pass envrc ports through locked lease allocation as preferred values rather than treating their presence as proof of an active reservation.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Revalidate doctor port conflicts after allocating replacement ports**

After `init` followed by `stop` or reap, another project's container can occupy a port retained in `.envrc.dopemux-mcp`. Doctor inspects that stale port before allocation, and this code retains its `DOCKER_CONTAINER_WRONG_PROJECT` finding even when `_resolve_ports()` successfully leases a different, free port. An isolated lifecycle reproduction returned `BLOCKED` with replacement port 3020 because a foreign container occupied the old envrc port 3040. Consequently, CLI starts and launcher cold starts cannot recover automatically despite successful rebinding. Recompute port-dependent doctor findings against the resolved ports, or replace them with the fresh collision checks instead of carrying them forward as immutable blockers.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Check marked runtime directories before skipping an empty registry**

On a fresh host where launches only reached `LAUNCH_IMAGE_BUILDING`, no instance records exist, but those launches leave marked runtime directories containing build logs and artifacts. If their worktrees are subsequently removed, this early return prevents every automatic reap from reaching `plan_reap()` and its `_dir_only_candidates()` recovery path—even after the builds finish. Those directories therefore accumulate until an explicit reap or an unrelated successful start creates a registry entry. Check for launcher-marked directories before treating an empty registry as proof that nothing needs cleanup.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Prefer active leases over stale envrc ports in status**

After `init`, then `stop` or reap, a subsequent start can lease replacement ports when another worktree occupies the old ones. Start leaves the informational envrc unchanged, but `status` calls this helper with `allocate=False`, bypassing lease reconciliation and returning the stale envrc ports. `_status_result()` consequently reports incorrect URLs and probes the old listener rather than the running sidecar. Read-only resolution should prefer matching active leases without allocating anything.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Forward runner cancellation to the backend request**

When a runner cancels an in-flight tool call, the proxy's server session cancels this forwarding coroutine, but SDK `ClientSession.send_request()` only removes its local response streams; it does not send a cancellation notification to the backend. An in-memory reproduction using the actual proxy and SDK returned `Request cancelled` to the runner while the backend subsequently committed its operation. Thus interrupted tool calls continue executing behind the new launcher proxy. Track the backend request ID and forward cancellation under a shielded cleanup scope.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve dry-run semantics during port allocation**

When `start --dry-run` or `restart --dry-run` runs without active leases, `_mutable_facts()` still passes `allocate=True` here. `_resolve_ports()` then invokes the allocator with `persist=True, dry_run=False`, creating active reservations even though no service starts. An isolated execution of the resolver confirmed that an informational envrc port creates a lease registry containing an active lease. These plan-only commands can therefore reserve ports needed by other worktrees or release and replace existing conflicting leases. Propagate the lifecycle's dry-run flag and use non-persisting allocation when planning.
